mewing.summary: Resting the whole tongue on the palate with lips closed and nasal breathing, aimed at a sharper jawline, more forward midface and better profile.

quick.overview:
Mewing is a posture habit: the whole tongue rests against the roof of the mouth, lips sealed, teeth lightly together, breathing through the nose. People do it for a more defined jawline, a more forward midface and a stronger side profile. It is named after British orthodontist John Mew and his son Mike Mew, and it spread through social media from 2019.

The idea is that the tongue's resting pressure guides upper-jaw growth forward, with the biggest effects claimed for people who start in childhood. Some users also say the posture lifts the area under the chin and tightens the jaw-neck line. The American Association of Orthodontists has stated there is no evidence it reshapes the jaw, and a 2019 commentary in the Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery said it is not an alternative to orthognathic surgery. The one controlled study usually cited was a small twin study of orthotropic appliances rather than tongue posture alone.
quick.how: People practise it as an all-day background habit rather than a workout: tongue up, lips closed, nose breathing, often paired with good head and neck posture, chewing and fat loss for a leaner lower face. Users typically report tracking progress with side-profile photos over months to years.
quick.risks: Gentle tongue posture is not documented to carry serious risks, though some online posts describe masseter enlargement or jaw tension from forceful versions. Orthodontic organizations warn it should not replace assessment for real bite or jaw problems. Mike Mew was struck off the UK dental register in 2024 over his clinical practice, which is separate from the home technique.

angle.text: Mewing aims at a more defined jawline, forward midface and better profile by keeping the tongue pressed to the palate with nasal breathing, an approach drawn from the orthotropics ideas of John and Mike Mew. Users report changes in side-profile photos; orthodontic bodies say tongue posture has not been shown to reshape adult facial bone.

hard-mewing.summary: Mewing with deliberate upward tongue pressure, used by people chasing faster jaw and midface change; some report bigger masseters.

quick.overview:
Hard mewing is a stronger version of mewing: instead of lightly resting the tongue on the palate, the person presses upward with deliberate effort. People use it hoping for a wider, more defined lower face, a more forward midface and better breathing and posture.

The reasoning extends the orthotropic idea that tongue pressure guides upper-jaw growth, with firmer pressure expected to do more. Bone does adapt to strain in general, but no published study has measured what forceful tongue pressure does to the adult face. Forum users most often report wider masseter muscles and a changed look to the cheeks.
quick.how: Users treat it as a step up from ordinary mewing, done in sessions or held through the day, and often combine it with chewing, chin tucks, thumb pulling or palate expanders. Reports of visible change in photos vary from weeks to years.
quick.risks: Forum users report enlarged masseters, altered cheek appearance, jaw or tongue fatigue, and a gap between the front teeth when combined with thumb pulling and expanders. These are anecdotal accounts; no clinical data exist on forceful tongue pressure, and orthodontic bodies note mewing in general has no supporting trials.

angle.text: Hard mewing is a forceful form of tongue posture used for faster jaw and midface definition, often alongside chewing, thumb pulling and expanders. Posters report wider masseters, which is a muscle change; bone change from tongue pressure has not been studied.

thumb-pulling.summary: Pulling the roof of the mouth downward and forward with a thumb, a free do-it-yourself attempt at widening the palate and bringing the midface forward.

quick.overview:
Thumb pulling means placing a thumb on the roof of the mouth and pulling down and forward, aiming for a wider palate, a more forward upper jaw, easier breathing and a fuller midface and smile. It is presented as a do-it-yourself imitation of orthodontic palate expanders.

The theory is that sustained force on the palate remodels bone, as expansion appliances do. Professional expansion uses fixed appliances applying controlled force over weeks, mostly in children and teens, because the midpalatal suture generally fuses after puberty. No published study has tested thumb pulling; some forum users report a sense of movement, others call it ineffective.
quick.how: Users usually do it in short daily sessions alongside mewing and chewing, and sometimes combine it with expanders. They commonly track changes by comparing smile and palate photos over months.
quick.risks: No clinical safety data exist for thumb pulling. Orthodontic literature on appliance expansion lists a gap between the upper front teeth, pain and bone thinning, and forum posts describe a front-tooth gap after combining thumb pulling with hard mewing and expanders. Hygiene and gag-reflex discomfort are other practical issues.

angle.text: Thumb pulling is used as a free stand-in for palatal expansion, aiming for a wider palate, more forward midface and fuller smile. It is usually paired with mewing and chewing; no study has tested it, whereas appliance-based expansion is an established orthodontic treatment.

chewing-for-jaw.summary: Chewing tough gum or hard food to build the masseters and give the lower face a wider, more defined look.

quick.overview:
Chewing for jaw, often called jawmaxxing, means chewing hard gum such as mastic or tough foods to build the masseters, the muscles at the angle of the jaw. The payoff people want is a wider, squarer, more defined lower face.

The masseter is a skeletal muscle and enlarges with sustained use; medical literature describes enlarged masseters in people who chew gum constantly, clench or grind their teeth. Whether chewing also changes the underlying jaw bone or profile has not been tested in published trials.
quick.how: Users chew mastic gum or firm foods in regular sessions, usually combined with mewing, chin tucks and neck exercises, and often with fat loss so the jaw shows. Visible muscle change is reported over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Medical sources link constant chewing and clenching to jaw muscle fatigue and temporomandibular symptoms, and a study of 323 adolescent girls examined gum chewing and jaw symptoms. Enlarged masseters can make the face look wider or uneven. One forum user reports worn molars and a bloated-looking face after years of chewing.

angle.text: Chewing tough gum or food builds the masseters, which can widen and define the lower face. Masseter enlargement from heavy chewing is documented in muscle research; effects on jaw bone have not been studied.

facial-yoga-face-exercises.summary: Routines of facial-muscle movements used as a natural facelift for firmer cheeks, a sharper jawline and a more lifted look.

quick.overview:
Facial yoga and face exercises are routines of deliberate facial-muscle movements, often taught on video, used for firmer cheeks, a sharper jawline and a lifted look around the eyes and mouth. People adopt them as a low-cost, non-surgical alternative to procedures.

The reasoning is that stronger facial muscles lift and fill the overlying skin, much as training builds other muscles. Small studies of facial exercise programmes in older adults have examined mental health and cognition rather than appearance. Forum users add that fat loss and chewing do more for facial shape, and describe the exercises as a fallback to surgery, appliances or fillers.
quick.how: People follow short daily routines of cheek lifts, jaw and brow movements, often alongside skincare, chewing and leaning out. Users generally describe results as gradual over weeks to months.
quick.risks: No documented harms appear in the sources used. Repeated strong expressions may deepen existing lines in some people, and a forum guide describes the exercises as less effective than surgery, appliances or fillers.

angle.text: Face exercises aim to tone the facial muscles for firmer cheeks, a sharper jaw and a more lifted look. Studies of facial exercise programmes have examined older adults' mental health rather than appearance, so results come mainly from practitioner and user accounts.

wolff-s-law-facial-loading.summary: The principle that bone adapts to load, cited as the logic behind mewing, chewing and pulling practices meant to reshape the jaw and cheekbones.

quick.overview:
Wolff's law is a nineteenth-century principle that bone adapts its structure to the loads placed on it. In looksmaxxing it is the reasoning behind mewing, chewing, thumb pulling and bonesmashing: if bone responds to load, then loading the face should build a stronger jaw and more prominent cheekbones.

The general principle, now usually called bone functional adaptation, is supported by research on limbs and the spine. Bone cells sense strain and signal bone-forming and bone-resorbing cells, and Frost's mechanostat model describes strain thresholds for adding or losing bone. Whether the small, specific forces of tongue posture, chewing or pulling change the adult facial skeleton has not been tested.
quick.how: People apply it by choosing practices that load the face, such as tongue posture, hard chewing or pulling on the palate, and by tracking changes in photos. It is a rationale rather than a routine of its own.
quick.risks: The principle itself carries no risk. Practices justified by it, such as forceful pulling or striking the face, have their own risks and are covered on their own pages.

angle.text: Wolff's law, the real principle that bone remodels to the loads it carries, is the logic behind mewing, chewing and pulling practices aimed at a stronger jaw and cheekbones. Applying it to adult facial bone with these methods has not been tested.

orbital-rubbing-eye-socket-massage.summary: Pressing or massaging around the eye socket in the hope of a more open, defined eye area without surgery.

quick.overview:
Orbital rubbing is a bonehack in which people press or massage the area around the eye socket, aiming for a more open, defined eye area and a change in how the orbit looks. It is discussed as a non-surgical option for eye-area aesthetics.

The idea is that sustained manual pressure remodels bone around the socket. The orbit is a rigid cavity formed by seven bones, and no clinical study has tested whether massage changes it; community material on the practice is sparse.
quick.how: Users describe light pressing or rubbing around the orbital rim in short daily sessions, sometimes alongside mewing and other bonehack routines, and judge results from eye-area photos over months.
quick.risks: Medical sources associate vigorous eye rubbing with progression of keratoconus, a corneal condition, and the orbit surrounds the eye and optic structures. Pressure near the eye has not been studied as a cosmetic technique.

angle.text: Orbital rubbing is used in the hope of a more open, defined eye area by pressing around the eye socket. No study has tested whether massage changes the orbital bones, and the practice is documented mainly in forum posts.

nose-bone-massaging-nasal-bone-pushing.summary: Pressing or massaging the nose bridge to narrow or straighten the nose without surgery.

quick.overview:
Nose bone massaging, or nasal bone pushing, is a bonehack in which people press or massage the nose, usually the bridge, hoping to narrow it, straighten it or change its shape without rhinoplasty.

The idea is that repeated pressure moves the nasal bones or the cartilage around them. The nasal bones are two small paired bones joined at the midline; medical literature about them concerns fractures and their surgical correction, and no clinical study has tested massage on healthy noses.
quick.how: Users describe gentle pressing or pinching of the bridge in short daily sessions, sometimes combined with other facial bonehacks, and compare front-on photos over months.
quick.risks: No studies have measured self-applied pressure on the nose. Trauma literature notes that an injured nose should be assessed for septal hematoma, which needs emergency treatment, so hard pressing or striking can cause injury.

angle.text: Users press or massage the nose bridge hoping for a narrower, straighter-looking nose without surgery. No study has tested it for reshaping; the medical literature on nasal bones concerns fractures and surgery.

hyoid-neck-posture-meta.summary: Raising the hyoid and correcting neck posture to sharpen the chin-to-neck angle and cleaner jawline in profile.

quick.overview:
The hyoid meta is the belief that a low hyoid bone, forward neck posture and submental fat blunt the angle between chin and neck. People work on it for a sharper under-chin line and a cleaner jawline in profile.

The hyoid is a horseshoe-shaped bone in the front of the neck, held by muscles and ligaments. Medical literature on its position concerns breathing and swallowing, and a lower hyoid is associated with obstructive sleep apnea. No study has tested whether exercises move the hyoid or change neck contour.
quick.how: Users combine chin tucks, neck and posture exercises and tongue posture with fat loss to reduce under-chin fullness, and check results in profile photos. Some also discuss submental injections or liposuction.
quick.risks: No harms are documented for the exercises themselves in the sources reviewed. Related procedures such as submental injections or liposuction are medical interventions with their own risks.

angle.text: The goal is a sharper chin-to-neck angle and cleaner profile through neck posture work, chin tucks and reducing under-chin fat. Hyoid research concerns airway anatomy, so the link to appearance comes from forum theory.

palate-expanders-adult.summary: Adult MARPE or surgically assisted palate expansion that widens the upper jaw for a fuller midface and smile, with better breathing as a common aim.

quick.overview:
Palate expanders widen the upper jaw. In adults, miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion (MARPE) or surgically assisted expansion is used for a narrow upper jaw, and looksmaxxers seek it for a wider midface, broader smile and easier breathing.

A screw-driven appliance anchored to the teeth, mini-implants in the palate, or both is turned to separate the midpalatal suture so new bone forms in the gap. Adults often need bone anchorage or surgical help because the suture has matured. Trials report skeletal expansion and some airway changes in selected patients; systematic reviews describe the evidence in late adolescents and adults as limited, and trials rarely measure facial attractiveness.
quick.how: It is delivered by orthodontists or oral surgeons: an appliance is fitted, adjusted at home over weeks, then held in place while bone fills in, usually followed by braces. Total treatment runs many months.
quick.risks: Reported effects include pain, speech changes, a gap between the front teeth, tongue sores, periodontal changes and variable success in adults. Surgical versions carry operative risks, and the work needs a qualified orthodontist.

angle.text: Adult expansion widens the upper jaw, which can broaden the dental arch, midface and smile. It is an established orthodontic procedure studied for narrow upper jaws and breathing; its effect on overall facial appearance has not been tested.

nasal-breathing-meta.summary: Breathing through the nose, sometimes with mouth taping, for better jaw and midface structure and a leaner, less bloated face.

quick.overview:
The nasal breathing meta is the habit of breathing through the nose instead of the mouth, with the goal of a stronger jaw and midface, a better profile and a less bloated face. It is closely tied to mewing, mouth taping and discussions of nasal surgery.

Proponents say breathing pattern and tongue posture influence the growing jaw and midface. Research links chronic mouth breathing in children to facial growth patterns, sometimes called long face syndrome, and a systematic review and meta-analysis examined its effect on facial skeletal development, though cause can run in either direction. Studies on adults who switch to nasal breathing are much thinner.
quick.how: Users make nose breathing a default during the day and exercise, add mouth tape at night, and pair it with mewing posture. People with blocked noses often look at the obstruction first, since nasal obstruction is a main cause of mouth breathing.
quick.risks: Breathing through the nose is normal physiology. Mouth taping is little researched and is described as risky for anyone with nasal blockage or sleep apnea. Nasal surgery such as turbinate reduction carries surgical risks, and some users raise empty nose syndrome.

angle.text: Users favour nasal breathing, sometimes with mouth taping, for a stronger jaw and midface and a leaner-looking face. Studies in children link mouth breathing to growth changes; whether switching as an adult changes appearance has not been tested.

sleeping-position-for-face-symmetry.summary: Sleeping on your back to avoid pressing one side of the face into the pillow and keep the face even.

quick.overview:
Back sleeping for symmetry is the habit of sleeping face-up so neither cheek is pressed into a pillow for hours. People do it for a more even-looking face and fewer sleep creases on one side.

The proposed mechanism is prolonged pressure on one side of the face during sleep. General references list development, aging and prenatal factors as causes of facial asymmetry, and list habitual sleeping position as one of several contributors to wrinkles; no study has measured sleep posture against facial symmetry.
quick.how: Users sleep on the back, sometimes with a contoured or flat pillow, a pillow wedge or a pillow under the knees to stay in position, and compare morning and long-term photos.
quick.risks: Sleep-position reviews note that back sleeping can worsen positional sleep apnea and snoring in some people. No other harms are documented for this practice.

angle.text: Sleeping on the back is meant to avoid pressing one cheek into the pillow and keep the face even and free of sleep creases. No study links sleep position to facial symmetry; general references name sleep posture only as one contributor to wrinkles.

cortisol-face-stress-face-claims.summary: The idea that stress hormones leave your face puffy, round and tired-looking, and that lowering stress gives a leaner, fresher look.

quick.overview:
'Cortisol face' is an informal term for a puffy, rounded or tired-looking face that people attribute to stress and elevated cortisol, the body's main stress hormone. The payoff people want from addressing it is a leaner, fresher, less swollen face.

In medicine, a rounded 'moon face' is a recognised sign of Cushing's syndrome, caused by prolonged exposure to excess glucocorticoids, most often from steroid drugs. Cortisol raises blood sugar, suppresses inflammation and increases sodium and water retention; with sustained high levels clinicians describe fat moving to the trunk and face, thinner skin and facial redness. Clinical sources tie this look to hormonal disorders, and no study has measured facial appearance against everyday stress.
quick.how: People use the idea to justify stress reduction, better sleep, lower alcohol and sodium intake and regular exercise for a leaner-looking face. In looksmaxxing forums, 'cortisol spikes' is also slang for stress or anxiety reactions.
quick.risks: Facial swelling, redness or rounding can have many causes, and Cushing's syndrome is diagnosed by clinicians with testing. Steroid medicines can themselves produce these facial changes, and some herbal supplements have been reported to contain undisclosed glucocorticoids.

angle.text: The goal is a leaner, less puffy face by lowering stress and its effects on fluid retention and fat distribution. Facial rounding is documented in medicine with sustained glucocorticoid excess; everyday stress has not been tested for this effect.

limb-lengthening-surgery-ll.summary: Surgery that cuts and gradually extends the femurs or tibias to add permanent height, with months of recovery and documented complications.

quick.overview:
Limb lengthening is an orthopaedic procedure in which a leg bone is cut and slowly pulled apart so new bone forms in the gap, adding permanent height. It was developed for limb-length differences, deformities and conditions such as achondroplasia, and is also performed electively by people who want to be taller. In looksmaxxing forums it is the best-known route to added stature beyond genetic potential.

The process, distraction osteogenesis, was developed by Gavriil Ilizarov: after a short healing period the segments are separated gradually, new bone and soft tissue form between them, and the bone then consolidates. Clinical series describe gains of several centimetres, mostly in medical patients, and the new bone is permanent.
quick.how: Methods include external frames and fixators, internal nails that lengthen mechanically or magnetically, and combinations. The bone lengthens over weeks, followed by months of consolidation and physiotherapy. Forum discussion centres on cost, surgeons, countries and recovery.
quick.risks: Reported problems include pin-site and deep infection, bone that fails to heal, deformity, hardware failure, joint stiffness, nerve injury and further operations. China's health ministry banned the procedure in 2006 after serious side effects, according to one encyclopedia summary, and cosmetic lengthening in India has been described as high-demand and largely unregulated. It is major surgery with a long rehabilitation.

angle.text: Limb lengthening adds permanent height by cutting and slowly extending the femurs or tibias, a measurable change in stature. The technique is established in medicine for limb discrepancy and deformity and is also performed electively for cosmetic height.

cosmetic-leg-lengthening-precice-nails.summary: Height surgery using a magnetically lengthened nail inside the bone instead of an external frame, adding permanent stature.

quick.overview:
The Precice nail is an implant placed inside a long bone after the bone is cut. A magnet held outside the leg remotely lengthens the nail in small daily steps, so the bone grows longer without an external frame and height increases permanently. It was developed for limb-length discrepancy, deformity correction and bone defects, and has been adopted for cosmetic lengthening in healthy adults.

The published literature is mostly case series and reviews in medical patients. Orthopaedic papers report accurate distraction and good bone healing. A 2025 meta-analysis compared external fixation with nailing for cosmetic lengthening, and a 2025 scoping review found studies capture clinical results better than quality-of-life outcomes.
quick.how: A surgeon cuts the femur or tibia and fixes the telescoping nail inside the canal; the patient then uses an external remote controller at home to lengthen it daily. Recovery involves weeks to months of limited weight-bearing and physiotherapy.
quick.risks: Reported problems include nail bending under load, failure of the bone to heal, joint stiffness and other complications, with some failures attributed to excessive loading. Surgeons describe it as demanding major surgery. Cosmetic use is elective and outside the device's usual medical indications.

angle.text: A magnetically driven nail inside the bone lengthens the leg in small steps without an external frame, adding permanent, measurable height. It is well studied for medical limb lengthening; cosmetic-specific data are newer.

hgh-for-height.summary: Growth hormone used to try to gain height; trialled in children with short stature for a few centimetres of added adult height.

quick.overview:
Human growth hormone (HGH, somatropin) is a prescription injectable used for growth hormone deficiency, Turner syndrome, chronic kidney disease and other conditions. 'HGH for height' means using it to get taller, either in children who are short without a hormone deficiency or, in looksmaxxing circles, by people hoping for height beyond their natural trajectory.

Growth hormone raises IGF-1 and stimulates growth at the growth plates of long bones in children and adolescents. In trials of children with idiopathic short stature, treatment over several years added about 4 to 8 cm of adult height in extreme cases, and about 5 to 8 cm in Turner syndrome. Paediatric papers debate the value of this as 'cosmetic endocrinology'. Height gain needs open growth plates, and no clinical trial identified has tested it in healthy adults with closed plates.
quick.how: In medicine it is prescribed and monitored by paediatric endocrinologists over years of treatment in children with open growth plates. Outside medicine, forum users discuss it for teenagers and adults, and also discuss growth-hormone-releasing peptides and IGF-1 analogues, which are separate and largely unstudied for height.
quick.risks: Documented effects include reduced insulin sensitivity and some cancer-subgroup signals in large studies, and a 2003 editorial said long-term risks in healthy people are unknown. Forum users report changes such as a widening nose, and costs can be very high. It is prescription-only in most countries, and counterfeit or mislabelled products have been reported in the gray market.

angle.text: Growth hormone raises IGF-1 and drives growth-plate activity, aiming at added height. Trials in children with short stature report gains of a few centimetres; use in healthy adults with closed growth plates has not been tested.

letrozole-aromatase-inhibitors-for-heigh.summary: Aromatase inhibitors used to slow bone maturation and extend the growing window in teens; trialled in boys with short stature.

quick.overview:
Aromatase inhibitors such as letrozole block the enzyme that converts androgens into oestrogen. Because oestrogen drives growth-plate closure, researchers have tested them in adolescent boys with short stature or delayed puberty, and height communities discuss them as a way to slow bone maturation and extend the growing window for extra height.

Lower oestrogen slows growth-plate fusion, which in theory leaves more time to grow. A meta-analysis of seven randomised trials, summarised in an encyclopedia entry, found letrozole safe and effective for improving height and puberty outcomes in children with constitutional delay of growth and puberty. A registered phase 3 trial tested aromatase inhibitors alone and with growth hormone in 76 adolescent boys with idiopathic short stature. No study identified tests them in healthy adults with closed plates.
quick.how: In medicine, paediatric specialists use them off-label in selected boys with open growth plates, sometimes alongside growth hormone, with bone-age monitoring. The drugs are approved mainly for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer.
quick.risks: Reference sources list hot flushes, joint pain and fatigue, with concern for bone density loss and raised cholesterol with long use, and note they are contraindicated in pregnancy. They are prescription-only in the US, UK and EU. Effects of use for height in healthy people are unstudied.

angle.text: Aromatase inhibitors lower oestrogen, slowing bone maturation and growth-plate closure to leave a longer window for growth. They have been trialled in boys with short stature and delayed puberty; use for height in healthy people is off-label.

hanging-stretching-for-height.summary: Bar hangs, traction and stretching to decompress the spine and recover a little standing height.

quick.overview:
Hanging and stretching for height means using bar hangs, traction or stretch routines to decompress the spine and recover or add a little standing height. It circulates in height-focused looksmaxxing spaces.

The idea is that gravity compresses the intervertebral discs through the day and sustained traction restores length. Reference sources describe daily height variation of around 1 to 1.5 cm, and radiographic studies of traction show temporary spinal elongation that largely reverses within about an hour. Height is largely genetic (60 to 80 percent heritability in twin studies), and no trial has tested lasting adult height gain.
quick.how: People hang from a pull-up bar, use traction or inversion devices, or do spine-lengthening stretches, often in the morning, before measuring, or before photos, and combine them with posture work.
quick.risks: Plain hanging is not specifically covered in the sources reviewed. Related inversion devices carry cautions for people with heart disease, hypertension, glaucoma or pregnancy.

angle.text: Hanging and stretching decompress the spine so the discs regain length, which can restore a little standing height. Brief increases in spinal length are reported after traction; a lasting gain in adult height has not been tested.

height-increasing-supplements.summary: Over-the-counter vitamin, mineral and herbal blends sold to help people grow taller or reach their genetic height potential.

quick.overview:
Height supplements are over-the-counter blends of vitamins, minerals, amino acids or herbs marketed to help people grow taller or reach their genetic height potential. Teenagers and adults ask about them in height-focused communities.

Marketers say the ingredients supply the nutrients growth needs. Reference sources describe height as strongly heritable (60 to 80 percent in twin studies) and influenced by childhood nutrition and health, and note that chronic malnutrition can stunt growth. No published trial of a marketed height supplement in healthy people was located.
quick.how: Products are taken daily as pills, powders or drinks, usually alongside sleep, protein-rich diet and exercise advice aimed at teenagers. Users often describe them as costly and slow.
quick.risks: No safety data specific to height supplements were located, and supplement contents are less tightly regulated than drugs. Prescription growth hormone is a separate, medically supervised treatment for short stature.

angle.text: Height supplements are sold as a way to supply the nutrients growth needs and reach your genetic height. Adequate nutrition supports normal growth in childhood; no trial of a marketed supplement for adding height has been located.

squatmaxxing-spinal-loading.summary: Squat-focused leg training that builds the quads and glutes for more balanced, athletic proportions.

quick.overview:
Squatmaxxing means training squats to build the quadriceps, glutes and lower body for more balanced, athletic proportions. Some users also ask whether it changes how tall or sturdy they look, and a looksmax.org thread discusses whether it suits people with a wide waist.

The squat is a compound exercise working the quadriceps, glutes, adductors and calves, with the spinal muscles and abdominals stabilising the trunk. Leg muscle growth from squatting is well established. The sources reviewed do not describe any effect on height, and spinal loading appears in height literature mainly through normal daily height variation.
quick.how: People add progressive squat training to a regular lifting routine, usually with leanness work so the legs and waist proportions show, and track changes in physique photos over months.
quick.risks: Wikipedia notes that poor form, especially over-flexing the torso, raises lower-back forces and can risk disc herniation. Heavy loading also compresses the spine temporarily.

angle.text: Heavy squat training builds the legs and glutes, giving more balanced, athletic proportions through added muscle. Leg growth from squatting is well established; no source ties squatting to a gain in height.
